evidence.quote: four different experimental alloy powders were prepared via vacuum induction melting and argon gas atomization.

An L-PBF (laser powder bed fusion) system (JHL100E +) equipped with an ytterbium fiber laser source was employed to fabricate the sample for microstructure characterization and mechanical property testing.

boron tends to segregate into the terminal liquid phase during solidification. This segregation promotes the formation of unstable liquid films in interdendritic regions, which are highly susceptible to tearing under solidification shrinkage stress.
uncontrolled B segregation and formation of low melting point Cr2B borides lead to severe hot tear cracking and poor printability in 0Nb and 0.72Nb alloys with low NbC/γ content.

an appropriate amount of primary (Nb, Ta)C/γ phase interfaces can promote a more uniform distribution of boron, reduce its enrichment in the interdendritic regions and suppress the formation of low melting point borides, thereby inhibiting hot tear cracking

The oversized, high-volume, and prematurely formed eutectic phases in the 2.11Nb alloy critically disrupt dendritic growth, potentially causing remelting. Simultaneously, their scale—comparable to interdendritic zones—severely impedes terminal liquid feeding.
